title: Developing and validating the Chinese version of the Perceived Trustworthiness of Large Language Models Scale (PT-LLM-8)
abstract: Abstract The trustworthiness of technology constitutes a critical determinant of user adoption, particularly regarding artificial intelligence (AI) in daily life. Currently, prominent AI products rely on large language models (LLMs), and such LLMs assist users in personal and professional contexts. To systematically investigate the perceived trustworthiness of LLMs, we provide a psychometrically sound measurement instrument for assessing perceived trustworthiness of LLMs. Given the importance of the Chinese market for current AI developments, the present study examined the psychometric properties of a Chinese version of the Perceived Trustworthiness of Large Language Models Scale (PT-LLM-8) [1] and its association with Big Five personality traits, self-efficacy, and self-esteem. Based on the responses of 478 Chinese adults, the Chinese PT-LLM-8 showed good psychometric properties, including strong internal consistency and a clear unidimensional factor structure. Evidence of construct validity was provided by theoretically expected associations between PT-LLM-8 score and self-efficacy, self-esteem, Agreeableness, and Conscientiousness. These findings provide psychometric support for the Chinese version of the PT-LLM-8 as a measure of perceived trustworthiness of LLMs, consistent with the cumulative cross-linguistic evidence for the instrument across its English [1], German [2] and Chinese versions.
